Front page

Residents pack hearing on proposed data center campus

More than two hundred residents filled the township meeting room on Saturday for a hearing on a proposed data center campus on farmland along the county road, with speakers raising concerns about noise, traffic and the demand the buildings would place on the regional electric grid.

The developer told the planning board that the first building would be finished within three years and that the campus would bring construction jobs and new tax revenue. Board members asked for additional studies of groundwater use and of the sound from cooling equipment at the property line.

The hearing was continued to a later date so the applicant can respond to questions from the board and the public. No vote was taken, and the board chair said written comments would be accepted until the next session.

Township officials said the application will also require review by the county soil conservation district and the state department of environmental protection before any permits can be issued.
